text_zh: 本寂禪師之於洞山。蓋瀉瓶而已。自一去不 變異處。至住持大法之道。則大與餘者別矣。 唯因真唱。使人至真證也。唯真也深玄精粹。 是以難卒見焉。世以為平坦無活用雄略。嗚 呼浮淺之人。胡知時世因真偽以致道之否 泰哉。實不知之。故有詖辭。夫師之語要。在三 墮示修治分位。異類通凡聖。明道之生熟也。 洞祖所言道合人人合道。老不老事體妙者 是也。苟知之不可瞞。只今唯瞞也多矣。元文 之間。有與洞山錄并行焉。而此亦不便多眾 之遮眼。庚辰之秋。吉祥之眾衲就予集錄焉。 刊版欲與洞祖錄并行。而以反正時世妄譌 也。可謂好心。冀有好報。且來請引語。乃敘 錄中至要。以冠其首。但因曹山意見其道範。 足一發其意云爾。維時
text_en: to the way of upholding the great Dharma, he was greatly distinct from the others. Only because he truly proclaimed did people reach true realization. Only what is true is profound, mysterious, and refined. Therefore it is difficult to fully perceive. The world takes him to be level and without lively function or heroic strategy. Alas, superficial people—how could they know that in any age, through truth and falsehood, the Way may flourish or decline? They truly do not understand; hence there are biased words. As for the essential points of the Master’s sayings, they lie in the Three Falls, which indicate the stages of cultivation and realization, bridging different kinds and communicating between ordinary and sage, clarifying the ripeness or immaturity of the Way. What Patriarch Dong said, “The Way accords with people, people accord with the Way; whether old or not old, the essential matter is subtle,” is precisely this. If one knows it cannot be concealed, yet nowadays concealment is indeed abundant. During the Yuanwen era, this record circulated alongside the Record of Dongshan; yet this too could not avoid being obscured by the multitude. In the autumn of the gengchen year, the assembly of monks at Jixiang requested that I compile this record. They carved the printing blocks, wishing it to circulate together with the Record of Patriarch Dongshan, in order to correct the delusions and errors of the times. It may be called a good intention, hoping for good recompense. They also came to request a preface. Thus I narrate the most essential points within the record and place them at its head. I only follow Caoshan’s intention in setting forth his model of the Way, merely giving voice to his meaning. At that time

text_en: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanzheng of Caoshan, Fuzhou Collated and edited by the distant descendant, Śramaṇa Huiyin The Master’s personal name was Benji. He was a son of the Huang family of Putian in Quanzhou. In youth he studied Confucianism. At nineteen

text_zh: 師諱本寂。泉州莆田黃氏子。少業儒。年十九 往福州靈石出家。二十五登戒。尋謁洞山。山 問。闍黎名甚麼。師曰本寂。山曰。向上更道。 師曰不道。山曰為什麼不道。師曰。不名本寂。 山深器之。自此入室。盤桓數載。乃辭去。山遂 密授洞山宗旨。復問曰。子向甚麼處去。師曰。 不變異處去。山曰。不變異處豈有去耶。師曰。 去亦不變異。遂往曹谿禮祖塔回吉水。眾嚮 師名。乃請開法。師志慕六祖。遂名山為曹。尋 值賊亂。乃之宜黃。有信士王若一。捨何王觀。 請師住持。師更何王為荷玉。由是法席大興。 學者雲萃。洞山之宗至師為盛。
text_en: he went to Lingshi in Fuzhou to leave home. At twenty-five he received the full precepts. Soon he visited Dongshan. Dongshan asked, “Venerable, what is your name?” The Master said, “Benji.” Dongshan said, “Say something beyond that.” The Master said, “I will not say.” Dongshan said, “Why will you not say?” The Master said, “It is not named Benji.” Dongshan deeply valued him. From then on he entered the inner chamber and remained for several years. Then he took his leave. Dongshan secretly transmitted the essential meaning of the Dongshan lineage. He further asked, “Where are you going?” The Master said, “To the unchanging place.” Dongshan said, “If it is the unchanging place, how can there be any going?” The Master said, “Even going does not change.” He then went to Caoxi to pay homage at the Patriarch’s stupa and returned to Jishui. The assembly, having heard of the Master’s name, invited him to open the Dharma. The Master admired the Sixth Patriarch and therefore named the mountain Cao. Soon there was bandit unrest, so he went to Yihuang. A faithful layman, Wang Ruoyi, donated He Wang Monastery and invited the Master to reside as abbot. The Master renamed He Wang as Heyu. Thus the Dharma seat greatly flourished. Students gathered like clouds. The Dongshan lineage reached its height with the Master.
A monk once asked about the essential formula of the Five Ranks of Lord and Minister. The Master said, “The proper rank is the realm of emptiness,

text_zh: 因有僧問五位君臣旨訣。師曰。正位即空界。 本來無物。偏位即色界。有萬象形。正中偏者 背理就事。偏中正者舍事入理。兼帶者冥應 眾緣。不墮諸有。非染非淨。非正非偏。故曰虛 玄大道無著真宗。從上先德推此一位最妙 最玄。當詳審辨明。君為正位。臣為偏位。臣向 君是偏中正。君視臣是正中偏。君臣道合是 兼帶語。進云。如何是君。師曰。妙德尊寰宇。 高明朗大虛。云如何是臣。師曰。靈機弘聖道。 真智利群生。云如何是臣向君。師曰。不墮諸 異趣。凝情望聖容。云如何是君視臣。師曰。妙 容雖不動。光燭本無偏。云如何是君臣道合。 師曰。混然無內外。和融上下平。師又曰。以君 臣偏正言者。不欲犯中。故臣稱君不敢斥言 是也。此吾法宗要。乃作偈曰。學者先須識自 宗。莫將真際雜頑空。妙明體盡知傷觸。力在 逢緣不借中。出語直教燒不著。潛行須與古 人同。無身有事超岐路。無事無身落始終。復 作五相。
text_en: originally without a single thing. The partial rank is the realm of form, with the forms of myriad phenomena. ‘The partial within the proper’ means turning one’s back on principle and entering into phenomena. ‘The proper within the partial’ means leaving phenomena and entering into principle. ‘The concurrently inclusive’ means responding mysteriously to all conditions, not falling into any existence, neither defiled nor pure, neither proper nor partial. Therefore it is said: The vast, mysterious great Way is the unattached true lineage. Since ancient times the former worthies have regarded this rank as the most wondrous and most mysterious. One must examine and discern it carefully. The lord is the proper rank; the minister is the partial rank. When the minister approaches the lord, this is the partial within the proper. When the lord regards the minister, this is the proper within the partial. When lord and minister accord in the Way, this is the language of concurrent inclusion.” The monk asked, “What is the lord?” The Master said, “Wondrous virtue honors the universe, lofty and bright, illuminating the great void.” He asked, “What is the minister?” The Master said, “Spiritual function broadens the sage’s Way, true wisdom benefits all beings.” He asked, “What is the minister approaching the lord?” The Master said, “Not falling into various different destinies, fixing one’s feeling in gazing upon the sacred countenance.” He asked, “What is the lord regarding the minister?” The Master said, “Though the wondrous countenance does not move, its light illumines without bias.” He asked, “What is the accord of lord and minister?” The Master said, “Merged without inside or outside, harmoniously level above and below.” The Master also said, “In speaking of lord and minister, partial and proper, it is so as not to violate the middle. Therefore the minister refers to the lord and does not dare to speak his name directly. This is the essential of my Dharma lineage.” He then composed a verse: “Students must first recognize their own lineage. Do not mix the true limit with stubborn emptiness. When the wondrous bright essence is fully known, it may cause harm upon contact; strength lies in meeting conditions without borrowing the middle. Speech should be such that even fire cannot burn it; in hidden conduct one must accord with the ancients. Without body yet having affairs, one transcends the forked roads; without affairs and without body, one falls into beginning and end.” He further made the Five Images. The verse says: “One in white robes must bow to the prime minister—this is not strange.

text_zh: 師行脚時。問烏石觀禪師。如何是毘盧師法 身主。烏石曰。我若向爾道即別有也。師舉似 洞山。山曰。好箇話頭秖欠進語。何不問為甚 麼不道。師却去進前語。烏石曰。若言我不道。 即瘂却我口。若言我道。即謇却我舌。師歸舉 似洞山。山曰古佛。
text_en: Wushi said, “If I were to tell you, there would then be something separate.” The Master reported this to Dongshan. Dongshan said, “A good topic, only lacking a further word. Why not ask why he does not speak?” The Master then went back and advanced the question. Wushi said, “If I say I do not speak, that would make me mute. If I say I speak, that would make me stammer.” The Master returned and reported this to Dongshan. Dongshan said, “Ancient Buddha” 。

text_zh: 師示眾曰。諸方盡把格則。何不與他道一轉 語令他不疑去。雲門在眾出問。密密處為甚 麼不知有。師曰。只為密密所以不知有。門云。 此人如何親近。師曰。莫向密密處親近。門云。 不向密密處時如何。師曰。始解親近。門云諾 諾。又問。不改易底人來。師還接不。師曰。曹 山無恁麼閑工夫。
text_en: so they leave without doubt?” Yunmen, among the assembly, came forth and asked, “In the most secret place, why is it that one does not know?” The Master said, “Just because it is most secret, therefore one does not know.” Yunmen said, “How does one draw near to this person?” The Master said, “Do not draw near in the most secret place.” Yunmen said, “If not in the most secret place, then how?” The Master said, “Only then do you understand drawing near.” Yunmen said, “Yes, yes.” He also asked, “If a person who does not change comes, will you receive him?” The Master said, “Caoshan has no such idle time.”

text_zh: 智炬到參問云。古人提持那邊人。學人如何 體悉。師曰。退步就己萬不失一。炬於言下頓 忘玄解。

Jinfeng Zhi arrived. The Master asked, “What have you come for?” Zhi said, “To build a hut.”

text_zh: 金峯志至。師問曰。作甚麼來。志曰。蓋屋來。 師曰。了也未。志云。這邊則了。師曰。那邊事 作麼生。志云。候下工日向和尚。師曰。如是如 是。
text_en: The Master said, “Is it finished?” Zhi said, “On this side it is finished.” The Master said, “What about the matter on that side?” Zhi said, “When the day’s work is done, I will come to the Master.” The Master said, “So it is, so it is.”

text_zh: 鏡清問。心徑苔生時如何。師曰。難得道音導者。 清云。向甚麼處去也。師曰只見苔生。不知向 甚麼處去。又問。清虛之理畢竟無身時如何。 師曰。理即如此。事作麼生。清云。如理如事。 師曰。謾曹山一人即得。爭奈諸聖眼何。清云。 若無諸聖眼。爭鑒得箇不恁麼。師曰。官不容 針。私通車馬。
text_en: Qing said, Where has it gone. The master said, One only sees the moss growing, and does not know where it has gone. He also asked, When, in the principle of pure emptiness, there is ultimately no body, how is it. The master said, The principle is just thus; but what about the concrete matter. Qing said, As the principle, so the matter. The master said, You may fool Caoshan alone, but what can you do about the eyes of all the sages. Qing said, If there were no eyes of the sages, how could one discern that which is not thus. The master said, Official law does not allow even a needle, yet in private carts and horses pass through.
The Master asked Elder De, "A bodhisattva in samadhi hears a fragrant elephant crossing the river. From what scripture does this come?"

text_zh: 師問德上座。菩薩在定聞香象渡河。出甚麼 經。僧云。出涅槃經。師曰。定前聞定後聞。僧 云。和尚流也。師曰。道也太殺道。始道得一 半。僧云。和尚如何。師曰。灘下接取。師又問。 佛真法身猶若虛空。應物現形如水中月。作 麼生說應底道理。德曰。如驢覰井。師曰。道則 太殺道。只道得八成。德曰。和尚又如何。師 曰。如井覰驢。
text_en: The monk said, "It comes from the Nirvana Sutra." The Master said, "Did he hear it before samadhi, or after samadhi?" The monk said, "Master, you are dragging me along." The Master said, "You speak too much indeed. You have only spoken half of it." The monk said, "How about you, Master?" The Master said, "Receive it below the rapids." The Master again asked, "The Buddha's true dharma-body is like empty space; responding to things, it manifests form like the moon in water. How do you explain the principle of response?" De said, "Like a donkey looking into a well." The Master said, "Said well enough, but too much said. You have only said eighty percent." De said, "How about you, Master?" The Master said, "Like the well looking at the donkey."
The Wayfarer in Paper Robes came to pay respects. The Master asked, "Are you not the Wayfarer in Paper Robes?" He said, "I dare not."

text_zh: 紙衣道者來參。師問。莫是紙衣道者否。云不 敢。師曰。如何是紙衣下事。道者云。一裘纔挂 體。萬法悉皆如。師曰。如何是紙衣下用。道者 近前應諾便立脫。師曰。汝秖解恁麼去。何不 解恁麼來。道者忽開眼問云。一靈真性不假 胞胎時如何。師曰。未是妙。道者云。如何是 妙。師曰。不借借。道者珍重便化。師示頌曰。 覺性圓明無相身。莫將知見妄疎親。念異便 於玄體昧。心差不與道為隣。情分萬法沈前 境。識鑒多端喪本真。如是句中全曉會。了然 無事昔時人。
text_en: The Master said, "What is the matter beneath the paper robe?" The Wayfarer said, "As soon as a single cloak is hung on the body, the ten thousand dharmas are all thus." The Master said, "What is the function beneath the paper robe?" The Wayfarer stepped forward, answered, and immediately died standing. The Master said, "You only know how to go like this. Why not know how to come like this?" The Wayfarer suddenly opened his eyes and asked, "When the one numinous true nature does not rely on womb or embryo, how is it?" The Master said, "That is not yet subtle." The Wayfarer said, "What is subtle?" The Master said, "Borrowing without borrowing." The Wayfarer bade farewell and passed away. The Master then showed a verse, saying: The awakened nature is perfectly bright, the formless body. Do not, through knowledge and views, vainly make near and far. When thought differs, then the mysterious body is obscured. When mind deviates, it is not neighbor to the Way. When feeling divides the myriad dharmas, one sinks into prior objects. With consciousness reflecting in many ways, the original truth is lost. If within such lines one fully understands, then clearly there is nothing to do, like the people of old.

text_zh: 僧舉。陸亙大夫問南泉。姓甚麼。泉曰姓王。亙 云。王還有眷屬也無。泉曰。四臣不昧。亙云。 王居何位。泉曰。玉殿苔生。問師。玉殿苔生意 旨如何。師曰。不居正位。僧云。八方來朝時 如何。師曰。他不受禮。僧云。何用來朝。師曰。 違則斬。僧云。違是臣分上。未審君意如何。師 曰。樞密不得旨。僧云。恁麼則燮理之功全歸 臣相也。師曰。爾還知君意麼。僧云。外方不敢 論量。師曰。如是如是。
text_en: said, "Does the king still have attendants or not?" Nanquan said, "The four ministers are not obscured." Lu said, "In what place does the king reside?" Nanquan said, "Moss grows in the jade hall." He asked the Master, "What is the meaning of 'moss grows in the jade hall'?" The Master said, "He does not dwell in the central seat." The monk said, "When the eight directions come to pay court, how is it?" The Master said, "He does not receive their homage." The monk said, "Then what use is there in coming to court?" The Master said, "Disobey, and you are beheaded." The monk said, "Disobedience belongs on the ministers' side. I have not yet heard how it is on the ruler's side." The Master said, "The privy council does not obtain his intent." The monk said, "Then the whole work of ordering and governing returns to the ministers and chancellors." The Master said, "Do you yet know the ruler's intent?" The monk said, "Those outside dare not discuss or measure it." The Master said, "Just so, just so."

text_zh: 僧問。學人通身是病。請師醫。師曰不醫。僧 云。為甚麼不醫。師曰。教汝求生不得求死不 得。
text_en: said, "Why do you not heal?" The Master said, "To make it so you cannot seek life, and cannot seek death either."
A monk asked, "The ancients said, 'I have a great illness, not healed by the world.' What illness is this,

text_zh: 僧問。古人曰。吾有大病。非世所醫。未審是甚 麼病。師曰。攢簇不得底病。僧云。一切眾生還 有此病也無。師曰。人人盡有。僧云。和尚還有 此病也無。師曰。此覓起處不得。僧云。一切眾 生為甚麼不病。師曰。一切眾生若病即非眾 生。僧云。未審諸佛還有此病也無。師曰有。僧 云。既有為甚麼不病。師曰。為伊惺惺。
text_en: exactly?" The Master said, "The illness that cannot be gathered together." The monk said, "Do all sentient beings also have this illness or not?" The Master said, "Every one of them has it." The monk said, "Does the Master also have this illness or not?" The Master said, "Here, no place of arising can be found." The monk said, "Why are all sentient beings not ill?" The Master said, "If all sentient beings were ill, then they would not be sentient beings." The monk said, "Do the Buddhas also have this illness or not?" The Master said, "They do." The monk said, "If they have it, why are they not ill?" The Master said, "Because they are awake."

text_zh: 云眾曰。僧家在此等衣線下。理須會通向上 事。莫作等閒。若也承當處分明。即轉他諸聖 向自己背後方得自由。若也轉不得。直饒學 得十成。却須向他背後叉手。說甚麼大話。若 轉得自己。則一切麁重境來。皆作得主宰。假 如泥裏倒地。亦作得主宰。如有僧問藥山曰。 三乘教中還有祖意也無。答曰有。僧云。既有 達磨又來作麼。藥山曰。只為有所以來。豈非 作得主宰轉得歸自己乎。如經云。大通智勝 佛十劫坐道場。佛法不現前。不得成佛道。言 劫者滯也。謂之十成亦云斷滲漏也。只是十 道頭絕矣。不忘大果故。云守住耽著名為取 次承當不分貴賤。我常見叢林好論一般兩 般。還能成立得事麼。此等但是說向去事露 布。汝不見。南泉曰饒汝十成猶較王老師一 線道也。大難事到此。直須仔細始得明白自 在。不論天堂地獄餓鬼畜生。但是一切處不 移易。元是舊時人。只是不行舊時路。若有忻 心。還成滯著。若脫得揀甚麼。古德云。只恐不 得輪迴。汝道作麼生。只如今人。說箇淨潔處。 愛說向去事。此病最難治。若是世間麁重事 却是輕。淨潔病為重。只如佛味祖味。盡為滯 著。先師曰。擬心是犯戒。若也得味是破齋。且 喚什麼作味。只是佛味祖味。纔有忻心便是 犯戒。若也如今說破齋破戒。即今三羯磨時 早破了也。若是麁重貪瞋癡雖難斷。却是輕。 若也無為無事淨潔。此乃重無以加也。祖師 出世亦只為這箇。亦不獨為汝。今時莫作等 閑。黧奴白牯修行却快。不是有禪有道。如汝 種種馳求覓佛覓祖乃至菩提涅槃。幾時休歇 成辦乎。皆是生滅心。所以不如黧奴白牯兀 兀無知。不知佛不知祖乃至菩提涅槃及以 善惡因果。但饑來喫草渴來飲水。若能恁麼 不愁不成辦。不見道。計較不成。是以知有。乃 能披毛戴角牽犁拽來。得此便宜始較些子。 不見彌勒阿閦及諸妙喜等世界。被他向上 人喚作無慚愧懈怠菩薩亦曰變易生死。尚 恐是小懈怠。在本分事合作麼生。大須仔細 始得。人人有一坐具地。佛出世侵他不得。恁 麼體會修行。莫趁快利。欲知此事。饒令成佛 成祖去也。只這是便墮三塗地獄六道去也。 只這是雖然沒用處。要且離他不得。須與他 作主宰始得。若作得主宰。即是不變易。若作 主宰不得。便是變易也。不見永嘉云。莽莽蕩 蕩招殃禍。問如何是莽莽蕩蕩招殃禍。曰只 這箇總是。云如何免得。曰知有即得。用免作 麼。但是菩提涅槃煩惱無明等總是。不要免。 乃至世間麁重之事。但知有便得。不要免。免 即同變易去也。乃至成佛成祖菩提涅槃。此 等殃禍為不小。因甚麼如此。只為變易。若不 變易。直須觸處自由始得。
text_en: all this. Do not treat it lightly. If where you take it up is clear, then you turn all the sages behind your own back, and only then are you free. If you cannot turn them, even if you learn it to the full ten parts, still you must stand behind them with folded hands. What big talk can you make? If you can turn it back to yourself, then when any coarse and weighty circumstance comes, you can be master of it all. Even if you fall to the ground in the mud, you can still be master. For example, a monk asked Yaoshan: In the teachings of the Three Vehicles, is there still the Patriarchs’ meaning or not? He answered: There is. The monk said: Since there is, why then did Bodhidharma come? Yaoshan said: Precisely because there is, he came. Is this not being master and turning it back to oneself? As the scripture says, Great Penetrating Wisdom Victory Buddha sat at the seat of enlightenment for ten kalpas; the Buddha Dharma did not appear before him, and he could not attain Buddhahood. The word kalpa here means obstruction. This is called tenfold completion, and also the cutting off of outflows. It is only that the ten avenues are cut off. Because one does not forget the great fruit, it is said: guarding and clinging to it is called grasping. Next, in taking it up there is no distinction of noble and base. I often see in monasteries people fond of discussing one kind and two kinds. Can they actually establish the matter? Such things are only talk about what lies ahead, spread out in the open. Have you not seen Nanquan say: Even if you reach tenfold completion, you still fall short of Teacher Wang by one thread. It is very difficult when the matter comes to this. You must be very careful before you can be clear and at ease. Do not speak of heaven, hell, hungry ghosts, or beasts; in every place, if you do not shift or change, you are originally the same old person, only you no longer walk the old road. If there is delighting in mind, it again becomes attachment. If you are free of it, what is there to choose? The ancients said: I only fear not getting to revolve through birth and death. Tell me, what does that mean? People nowadays just speak of a pure and clean place. They love to speak of what lies ahead. This sickness is the hardest to cure. As for worldly coarse and weighty things, those are light. The sickness of purity and cleanliness is heavy. As for the taste of Buddha and the taste of the Patriarchs, all of it becomes obstruction and attachment. My former teacher said: To stir up a contrived mind is to break the precepts. To get a taste of it is to break the fast. Now what do you call taste? It is simply the taste of Buddha and the taste of the Patriarchs. The moment there is a mind of delight, that is breaking the precepts. If you now speak of breaking the fast and breaking the precepts, then right now at the time of the three karmas they were already broken long ago. Coarse greed, anger, and delusion may be hard to cut off, but they are still light. But if it is non-doing, no concerns, purity and cleanliness, this is heavy beyond anything more. The Patriarchs came into the world only for this, and not for you alone. At this time do not treat it as casual. The black slave and white ox practice more swiftly. It is not that they have Chan or the Way. But as for you, chasing in all ways, seeking Buddha, seeking Patriarchs, even seeking bodhi and nirvana, when will you ever stop and accomplish it? All of that is a mind of arising and ceasing. Therefore it is not as good as the black slave and white ox, standing there blank and unknowing, not knowing Buddha, not knowing Patriarchs, not even bodhi or nirvana, nor good and evil, cause and effect. They simply eat grass when hungry and drink water when thirsty. If you can be like this, do not worry that it will not be accomplished. Have you not heard it said: Calculating does not succeed. Therefore by knowing there is, one can then wear fur and horns, be led by the plow and pull it along. Gaining this advantage, you are at last somewhat close. Have you not seen that Maitreya, Akshobhya, and all those wondrous joyful worlds are called by those people of the beyond shameless and lazy bodhisattvas, and also called transformation birth-and-death. One still fears that this is only a small laziness. In the matter that is one’s own proper share, how should it be? You truly must be careful before you get it. Everyone has a ground for a sitting mat. Even a Buddha appearing in the world cannot encroach upon it. If you understand and practice in this way, do not chase quick profit. If you wish to know this matter, even if you become a Buddha or become a Patriarch, just this is what makes you fall into the three evil paths, hell, and the six realms. Though this very thing is of no use, still you cannot leave it. You must become its master before it will do. If you can be master of it, then there is no transformation. If you cannot be master, then it is transformation. Have you not seen Yongjia say: Vast and heedless, drifting about, one invites disaster. Someone asked, What is this vast heedless drifting that invites disaster? He said: Just this altogether is it. He asked: How can one avoid it? He said: Knowing there is is enough. What need is there to avoid anything? Bodhi, nirvana, affliction, ignorance and the rest are all this. Do not try to avoid them. Even worldly coarse and weighty matters are the same. Just know there is, and that is enough. Do not avoid them. To avoid them is to go along with transformation. Even becoming Buddha, becoming Patriarch, bodhi, nirvana — these disasters are not small. Why is it like this? Only because of transformation. If there is no transformation, then you must be free wherever you touch, and only then is it attained.

text_zh: 上堂僧問。如何是大闡提人。師曰。不懼業。僧 云。如何是無明人。師曰。始終不覺悟。僧云。 此二人誰在前。師曰。無明者。僧云。闡提人為 什麼在後。師曰。向去者。僧云。恁麼則無明者 不從今日去也。師曰是。僧云。既不從今日去。 無明從何處來。師曰。光處不敢入。僧云。豈不 是不明不暗。師曰是。僧云。正恁麼時如何。師 曰。不受觸。師復曰。闡提有多種。一類者是殺 父殺母。出佛身血。破和合僧。毀壞伽藍。此剋 定實報受種種苦。一類者亦所作如前。此則 為殺無明父貪愛母。不信有佛法僧可破。有 伽藍可壞。計為業心所得。故墮亦受種種虛 妄果報如前。升降不同。一類者知有自己本 來事。呼為父母。不因外得。無修無證。非因非 果。不因師受。不從證行所得。不起父見曰殺。 不起母見曰害。即是一切本分事不敢不存。 故曰殺害。纔有纖毫奉重得味。不成知有自 己事也。故曰大闡提。以此動撥妙力。即是從 上宗乘體會家事承當。要截玄道破諸迂曲。 即如新豐老人所玄示也。
text_en: said: What is a person of ignorance? The master said: One who from beginning to end does not awaken. The monk said: Which of these two is prior? The master said: The one of ignorance. The monk said: Why is the icchantika person later? The master said: The one going onward. The monk said: Then the one of ignorance does not depart starting today? The master said: Yes. The monk said: Since he does not depart from today, where does ignorance come from? The master said: It does not dare enter where there is light. The monk said: Then is it not neither bright nor dark? The master said: It is. The monk said: At just such a time, what then? The master said: It does not receive contact. The master then added: There are many kinds of icchantika. One kind is one who kills father and kills mother, draws the Buddha’s blood, breaks up the harmonious sangha, and destroys monasteries. This kind surely receives real retribution and undergoes all kinds of suffering. Another kind also does as above, but this one takes ignorance as father and craving love as mother and kills them. He does not believe there is Buddha, Dharma, or Sangha to be broken, nor a monastery to be destroyed. Yet he calculates that these are attained by karmic mind, and so falls and receives all kinds of false retributions like the former one, though the rise and fall differ. Another kind knows there is one’s own original matter, and calls it father and mother. It is not obtained from outside. There is no cultivation and no realization, neither cause nor result. It is not received from a teacher, nor gained from realization and practice. Not giving rise to a view of father is called killing. Not giving rise to a view of mother is called harming. This is to not dare fail to preserve the whole matter that is one’s own proper share. Therefore it is called killing and harming. If there is even the slightest honoring, weighting, or getting a taste, then one does not truly know there is one’s own matter. Therefore it is called the great icchantika. To stir and apply the subtle power in this way is precisely the family task realized and borne from the highest vehicle of the school. It is meant to cut off the dark path and smash all crooked byways. This is just what the old man of Xinfeng darkly indicated.

He himself answered in his place, All day long it is behind one’s back, and has never been seen.

text_zh: 俱胝和尚凡有詰問唯舉一指。後有童子。因 外人問。和尚說何法要。童子亦竪起一指。胝 聞遂以刃斷其指。童子負痛號哭而去。胝復 召之。童子回首。胝却竪起指。童子忽然領悟。 胝將順世。謂眾曰。吾得天龍一指頭禪。一生 用不盡。言訖而寂。師曰。俱胝承當處莽鹵。只 認得一機一境。
text_en: an outsider asked, What Dharma essential does your master teach. The boy also held up one finger. Judi heard of it and then cut off his finger with a blade. The boy, bearing the pain, wailed and ran away. Judi again called him. The boy turned his head. Judi then raised a finger. The boy suddenly awakened. When Judi was about to pass away, he told the assembly, I obtained Tianlong’s one-finger Chan, and in a whole lifetime could not exhaust its use. Having said this, he passed away. The Master said, Judi was crude where he undertook it. He only recognized one function and one condition.
A monk asked, Vimalakirti remained silent and Manjusri praised it as good. I wonder whether that still accords with Vimalakirti’s

text_zh: 僧問。維摩默然文殊讚善。未審還稱得維摩 意麼。師曰。爾還縛得虛空麼。僧云。恁麼則不 稱維摩意也。師曰。他又爭肯。僧云。畢竟有 何所歸。師曰。若有所歸即同彼二公也。僧云。 和尚又作麼生。師曰。待爾患維摩病始得。
text_en: meaning. The Master said, Can you bind empty space. The monk said, If so, then it does not accord with Vimalakirti’s meaning. The Master said, And why would he agree to that. The monk said, In the end, is there any place to return to. The Master said, If there is somewhere to return, then it is the same as those two gentlemen. The monk said, Then how is it for the master? The Master said, Wait until you fall ill with Vimalakirti’s illness, then it may be so.
On a summer night in the Xinyou year of Tianfu, the Master asked the steward, What day and month

text_zh: 師於天復辛酉夏夜問知事曰。今日是幾何 日月。對云。六月十五。師曰。曹山平生行脚。到 處秖管九十日為一夏。明日辰時吾行脚去。 及時焚香宴坐而化。閱世六十二。臘三十七。 葬全身於山之西阿。諡元證禪師。塔曰福圓。
text_en: is today. He replied, The fifteenth day of the sixth month. The Master said, All my life, when traveling, Caoshan has only reckoned ninety days as one summer retreat wherever I went. Tomorrow at chen hour I will travel on. When the time came, he burned incense, sat upright in composure, and transformed. He lived sixty-two years in the world, and had thirty-seven years since ordination. They buried his whole body on the western slope of the mountain. He was posthumously titled Chan Master Yuanzheng. His stupa was named Fuyuan.

text_zh: 解釋洞山五位顯訣自下本光重編
text_en: Explanation of Dongshan’s Clear Instructions on the Five Ranks Recompiled by Ben Guang A separate selection says: As for what the former master clarified regarding the partial and the upright, and the combined and contiguous, all employs the former

text_zh: 別時揀云。夫先師所明偏正與兼帶。等用先 師本意。不為明功進修之位兼涉教句。直是 格外玄談要絕妙旨。秖明從上物體現前。冥 叶古聖之道。今見諸學士詮揀先人意度。似 有誤彰音障不免聊為敘其差。當媿音貴在不混其 功。於中或有借位明功借功明位。緣緒多端。 功在臨時。看語來勢。不負來機。妙在佳致 爾。
text_en: master’s original intent. It was not to clarify ranks of meritorious cultivation and progress, nor to involve doctrinal phrases. It is directly a mysterious discourse outside conventions, whose essential point is wondrous and ultimate. It only clarifies the manifestation of the thing itself from above, in hidden accord with the way of the ancient sages. Now I see various scholars interpreting and sorting the former worthies’ intention and measure, and it seems there are mistaken displays. I cannot avoid briefly setting forth their differences. One should be ashamed not to mix up their Pronounced zhang Pronounced gui functions. Within this there are cases of borrowing rank to clarify function and borrowing function to clarify rank, with many different threads. Function is in the moment at hand. Look at the force with which the words come. Do not fail the incoming occasion. The subtlety lies in apt finesse like this.
The upright rank yet partial. Within the partial one discerns two meanings, namely completeness. Sorted rank by rank, it is brought out:

text_zh: 正位却偏。就偏辨得是圓兩意　逐位揀出 曰。正位却偏者。為不對物。雖不對物却具 　別揀曰。正位却偏。正中無用為偏。全用為圓。 是兩意問如何是全。云不頑者得底人也。此 位不明來也。若佛出世也恁麼。若佛不出世 也恁麼。所以千聖萬聖皆歸正位承當　別 時揀曰。正中偏却具。此一位。第一不得動 著。
text_en: It says, The upright rank yet partial means not confronting things. Though not confronting things, it nevertheless possesses A separate selection says: The upright rank yet partial means within the upright, no functioning is partial; total functioning is complete. These are the two meanings. Asked, What is total. It says, The person who has attained and is not dull. In this rank, coming is not made explicit. If a Buddha appears in the world, it is thus. If a Buddha does not appear in the world, it is also thus. Therefore thousands and myriads of sages all return to the upright rank to undertake it. Separate selection says: In the upright, the partial is nevertheless fully present. In this rank, above all one must not stir it.
The partial rank, though partial, is also complete in two meanings. Within conditions one discerns it as speech within no-speech

text_zh: 偏位雖偏亦圓兩意。緣中辨得是有語中無 語　逐位揀曰。偏位雖偏亦圓兩意者。為用 處不立的的。的的則真不常用也　別揀曰。 偏位雖偏亦圓者。用中無物無觸。是兩意雖 就用中明。為語中不傷。此乃竟日道如不道 　別時揀曰。偏位却圓亦具緣中不觸。
text_en: Rank-by-rank selection says: The partial rank, though partial, is also complete in two meanings, because at the place of functioning there is no fixed exactness. If exactness were fixed, the true would not be in constant use. A separate selection says: The partial rank, though partial, is also complete, because in functioning there is no thing and no contact. These are the two meanings. Though clarified within functioning, in speech they do not injure. Thus all day long speaking is like not speaking. A separate selection says: The partial rank yet complete also fully possesses non-contact within conditions.
There are also cases of coming from within the upright rank. This is speech within no-speech. Rank-by-rank selection

text_zh: 或有正位中來者。是無語中有語　逐位揀 曰。正位中來者。不兼緣。如藥山云。我有一句 子。未曾向人說。道吾云。相隨來。此是他妙會 得。如湖南觀察使語。此例甚多。須合出不 得混尊卑。呼為無語中有語　別揀曰。正位 中來者。句句無語。不立尊貴。不落左右。故云 正中來也。又引正中來語例者。如黑豆未生 芽時作麼生。又引一句子未曾向人說。又如 云有一人無出入息。又云未具胞胎時還有 言句也無。此例亦多。喚作無語中有語　別 時揀曰。正位來明正位不涉緣。亦有正位中 來。無語中有語如云黑豆未生芽時。十方諸 佛出身處。又我有一句子。未曾向人說。此句 答家須就出不得乖角。乖角則不知有故。
text_en: says: Coming from within the upright rank does not combine with conditions. For example, Yaoshan said, I have one phrase I have never spoken to anyone. Daowu said, Bring it along and come. This is his wondrous understanding attained. As with the words of the Hunan Inspector, there are many such examples. They must be distinguished and brought out, and one must not confuse higher and lower. This is called speech within no-speech. A separate selection says: The upright rank coming from within means every phrase is no-speech. It does not establish nobility and does not fall to either side. Therefore it is called coming from the upright. Also, examples of sayings from within the upright include: When black beans have not yet sprouted, how is it. Also the saying, I have one phrase never spoken to anyone. Also such sayings as There is one person without inhalation or exhalation. Also, before the embryo is fully formed, is there still any speech or not. There are many such examples. They are called speech within no-speech. Separate selection says: Coming from the upright clarifies that the upright rank does not involve conditions. There is also coming from within the upright rank, speech within no-speech, as in saying: before black beans sprout; the place from which the Buddhas of the ten directions emerge. And also, I have one phrase I have never spoken to anyone. These phrases must be answered by the respondent accordingly and without angular deviation. If one deviates, one does not know what is there.
There are also cases of coming from within the partial rank. This is no-speech within speech. Rank-by-rank selection

text_zh: 或有偏位中來者。是有語中無語　逐位揀 曰。偏中來者則兼緣。如云即今往來底喚作 甚麼則得。洞山云不得不得。此例亦多。呼為 有語中無語　別揀曰。偏位中來者。語從 四大聲色中來。不處所是非。故云緣中辨得 是偏位中來也。又引偏位中來語例者。如云 甚麼物恁麼來。亦云光境俱忘復是何物。亦 云定慧等學明見佛性。此例亦多。喚作有語 中無語。更有挾功極則。呼為偏位中來。此難 辨。須揀得出　別時揀曰。偏位來明偏位涉 緣。緣性無體皆同正位。偏位中來者。就物明 體。如云甚麼物恁麼來。亦云光境俱忘復是 何物。此一例語寄功明位。余舊舉。又甚麼物 恁麼來。此一例語雖緣中得。不同向去。又如 定慧等學明見佛性。此一例語亦余初舉例 語。又如光境俱忘。為是教中之則。不同玄學。 只要於他教則出宗門中玄學外事。秖如出 息不依眾緣。入息不居蘊界而住。此語全是 功不同緣中認得。亦是余舊舉例。亦主家抽 入正位云。有一人無出入息。令渠知有正位。 又有借事正位中來者。此一位答家須向偏 位中明其物體。不得入正位明也。此一句要 如。先師問新羅僧。未過海時在甚麼處。無對。 自代云。秖今過海也甚麼處。又如先師代慎 微長老出拄杖語云。如今出也有人辨得麼。 此例雖緣中認得。不同向去。辨不得。恐後人 收落功勳。將為向上事。
text_en: says: Coming from within the partial then combines with conditions. For example, saying: That which now comes and goes, what shall it be called so that it is right. Dongshan said, Not permissible, not permissible. There are many such examples. This is called no-speech within speech. A separate selection says: Coming from within the partial rank means speech comes from the four great elements and from sound and form. It does not dwell in right and wrong. Therefore it is said: within conditions one discerns this as coming from within the partial rank. Examples of sayings from within the partial rank include: What thing comes thus. Also, when both light and object are forgotten, what thing is it then. Also cultivating samadhi and wisdom equally makes one clearly see Buddha-nature. There are many such examples. They are called speech with no-speech within it. There are also cases carrying function to the ultimate, called coming from within the partial rank. These are hard to distinguish and must be sorted out. A separate selection says: Coming from the partial clarifies that the partial rank involves conditions. The nature of conditions has no substance and all alike return to the upright rank. Coming from within the partial rank means clarifying the body through things. As in saying, What thing comes thus. Also, when both light and object are forgotten, what then is the thing. This class of examples lodges function to clarify rank, as I formerly cited. Again, What thing comes thus. Though this type of saying is attained within conditions, it is not the same as going onward. Again, as in cultivating samadhi and wisdom equally and clearly seeing Buddha-nature, this type of saying too is among my earlier cited examples. Also, as for both light and object forgotten, that is a rule within doctrine and is not the same as mysterious learning. One only needs to bring it out from within those doctrinal rules into the Chan gate’s matter beyond speculative learning. For example, exhalation does not rely on manifold conditions; inhalation does not abide in the aggregates and realms. This saying is wholly function and is not something recognized within conditions. This too is one of my former examples. It also lets the host draw it into the upright rank, saying: There is one person without inhalation or exhalation, making him know there is an upright rank. There are also cases of borrowing an affair for coming from within the upright rank. In this rank, the respondent must from the side of the partial clarify its body. One must not enter the upright rank to explain it. This phrase must be like this: The former master asked a Silla monk, Before crossing the sea, where were you. He had no reply. He answered in his place, Right now crossing the sea, where is it. Also, the former master answered for Elder Shenwei when he presented the staff, saying: Now that it is brought forth, is there anyone who can discern it. Though these examples are recognized within conditions, they are not the same as going onward. If they are not distinguished, I fear later people will gather them into meritorious traces and take them for the matter above.
There are also cases of coming with mutual combination and contiguity. Here one does not speak of speech or no-speech. Within speech

text_zh: 或有相兼帶來者。這裡不說有語無語。語裡 直須正面而去。這裡不得不圓轉。事須圓轉。 然在途之語總是病。夫當人先須辨得語句 正面而去。有語是恁麼來。無語是恁麼去。作 家中不無言語。不涉有語無語。這箇喚作兼 帶語。全無的的也。他智上座臨遷化時向人 道。雲巖不知有。我悔當時不向伊說。雖然如 是。且不違於藥山蔡子。看他智上座合作麼 生老婆也。南泉喚作異類中行。且密闍黎不 知　逐位揀曰。相兼帶來者。為語勢不偏不 正不有不無。如全不全似虧不虧。唯得正面 而去也。則的不立。的不立則至妙之言。境不 圓常情之事也。如先師對文殊喫茶語云。借 取這箇看得麼。亦如翠微云。每日噇甚麼。亦 有功勳中兼帶。似向上事。臨時辨取。如落淨 妙之處。則須知有事在。要去則去。要止則止。 千萬圓轉不得莽鹵。如大無明底人。為全體。 不同闡提。闡提則知有事却鞔。雖鞔却成孝 養。鞔者不存祖佛及自己本分父母也。紅爛 底人為不歸全擔荷。不立至尊。大保任底人 為刺脚入泥裡。非小小護持　別揀曰。相兼 帶來者。不落有語無語。如藥山帶刀語。此是 兼帶語。臨時看語來勢。或當頭正面而去。或 異中虛句此句若不妙會。則千里萬里也。又引 相兼帶來語例。如文殊喫茶語兼這箇人甚麼 處去也。雲巖云作麼作麼。又云即今作麼生。 此例甚多　別時揀曰。相兼帶不涉偏正二 途。此一位等絕。妙旨難辨。呼為兼帶。皆為 明這箇一段事。況復正位不同　學士揀曰。 問祖師意。答待特牛生兒則向汝說。揀云此 是正位中來。此一例語切不得呼為正位中 來。可云玄學路中問答。俱然也。別是一路。又 不得呼為相兼帶。為顯明故。縱賓主回互。亦 秖得呼為有病兼帶。又問玄旨。答如死人舌。 又如問十二時中將何奉獻云無物。此二例 語不得呼為偏位中來。須各揀。若是玄旨一 例語可同於祖師意也。又如十二時中將何 奉獻答無物。此一例語可同於功勳也。此二 例語竝不得呼為偏位及兼帶也。前已明破 了。是借功明位。借位明功。同於此也。又獨脫 物外。起眾聖前。云是正位却圓。其實屈正位 也。此例是古人道過跡尚在。猶未得語中無 語。此復呼為非正位也。為語中有語故。此可 呼為有病兼帶。為語中有語故。不得呼為相 兼帶來。夫相帶兼來者。直須似文殊喫茶語。 及先師答雲巖鉏薑語。竝安和尚法堂語。及 藥山布衲洗佛語。於中最妙兼帶無過藥山 答雲巖帶刀語。及百丈下堂。大眾欲散未散 時。索云。是甚麼。藥山遙聞此語云在此。便道 暗頭兼帶。借功明物。借物明功。借過明功。借 功明過。等來。若是藥山與新豐竝前諸德所 出。超過入正位。是玄談奇特句已。次到小小 得力者。即且抽入正位。此例吾常用也。吾緣 住持多緒。不及子細。略明少分許。汝等諸人 不須容易輕慢。若更有疑帶。旋當決了。直須 厲力修行令未來際不斷。此事不得慢洩。或 值純忖者。是奇器也。亦不可隱耳。
text_en: one must go straight by the front face. Here one cannot avoid complete turning. The matter must turn completely. Still, words while on the road are all sickness. A person must first discern the front face of the phrases and then go on. Speech comes thus. No-speech goes thus. In the house of adepts, there is not no speech, yet it does not involve speech or no-speech. This is called combined contiguity speech. It is wholly without fixed exactness. When Senior Monk Taizhi was nearing death, he said to people He said, "Yunyan did not know there was such a thing. I regret that at the time I did not tell him." Even so, though it is thus, it still does not go against Yaoshan's intent. Look how Senior Monk Zhi was to act as an old granny. Nanquan called this "moving among other kinds." Moreover, Master Mi did not know. In the item-by-item selections he said: "What comes with mutual inclusion is speech-force neither biased nor upright, neither existent nor nonexistent. Like complete yet not complete, like lacking yet not lacking. One only attains the direct face and goes forth. Then the target is not established. When the target is not established, this is supremely subtle speech. The realm is not rounded according to ordinary feeling. For example, the late master in the Manjusri tea-drinking saying said, "Borrow this and see if you can see." It is also like Cuiwei saying, "What do you eat every day?" There is also inclusion within merit-function. It resembles the matter of going upward. At the moment, discern it. As for the point where one falls into pure subtlety, one must know there is something there. If one wants to go, then go. If one wants to stop, then stop. In all ways, turning and revolving must not be crude. As for one deeply in ignorance, it is because of the whole body. This is not the same as an icchantika. An icchantika knows there is something, yet covers it over. Though covered over, it still becomes filial support. One who covers it over does not preserve the patriarchs and buddhas, nor one's own original father and mother. A rotten-red sort of person fails to return and wholly bear it, and does not establish the utmost honored one. One of great preserving-and-trusting is one who pricks the feet and enters the mud. It is no small protection and support. Another selection says: mutual inclusion and carrying-along does not fall into speech or no-speech. Like Yaoshan's "wearing a sword" saying, this is an inclusion-saying. At the moment, look at the force with which the words arrive. Sometimes it goes straight at the head, face-on. Sometimes within otherness it is empty. If this is not subtly understood, then it is a thousand miles, ten thousand miles away. It also cites line line examples of sayings that come with mutual inclusion, like the Manjusri tea-drinking saying, and "Where has this person gone?" Yunyan said, "How? How?" And again said, "Right now, how is it?" There are many examples like this. Another time a selection said: mutual inclusion does not involve the two paths of bias and uprightness. This one position is cut off from all comparisons. The subtle meaning is hard to distinguish. It is called inclusion, all for clarifying this single matter. How much more so since the upright position is not the same. A scholar's selection says: Asked, "What is the Patriarch's meaning?" Answer: "When a barren cow gives birth, then I will tell you." The selection says this comes from within the upright position. This example of speech absolutely must not be called "coming from within the upright position." It may be called question and answer on the road of dark learning. Both are so. It is a separate route. Again, it must not be called mutual inclusion, for the sake of clarity. Even if host and guest interchange, it can only be called flawed inclusion. Again, asked about the dark meaning, answer: "Like a dead man's tongue." Again, as when asked, "Throughout the twelve hours, what is offered?" and the answer was, "No thing." These two examples of speech must not be called coming from the biased position. Each must be distinguished. As for the "dark meaning" example, that speech-example may be grouped with the Patriarch's meaning. Again, as in "Throughout the twelve hours, what is offered?" answer: "No thing." This example of speech may be grouped with merit-function. These two examples must not be called either the biased position or inclusion. This was already clearly refuted before. They are "borrowing function to clarify position" and "borrowing position to clarify function," the same as this. Again, "alone released beyond things, rising before the multitude of sages" is called the upright position, yet complete. In truth, it bends the upright position. This example is such that the traces remain after the ancients spoke it. It still has not attained no-speech within speech. Therefore this is again called not the upright position, because within the speech there is speech. This may be called flawed inclusion, because within the speech there is speech. It must not be called mutually inclusive carrying-along. As for what comes with mutual carrying and inclusion, it must be just like the Manjusri tea-drinking saying, and the late master's reply to Yunyan's hoeing-ginger saying, and Master An's dharma-hall saying, and Yaoshan's patched-robe monk washing the Buddha saying. Among these, the finest inclusion is none beyond Yaoshan's reply to Yunyan's "wearing a sword" saying. And when Baizhang descended the hall, as the assembly was about to disperse but had not yet dispersed, Suo said, "What is this?" Yaoshan heard these words from afar and said, "Here." Then one can speak of hidden-head inclusion: borrowing function to clarify the thing, borrowing the thing to clarify function, borrowing transgression to clarify function, borrowing function to clarify transgression, and the like. As for what was brought out by Yaoshan, Xinfeng, and the various worthies before them, it surpasses and enters the upright position. These are dark-discourse, extraordinary phrases already. Next, when it comes to those with only slight attainment of power, then for the moment draw it into the upright position. This kind of example I often use. Because I, due to the many affairs of abbacy, cannot go into fine detail, I have only roughly clarified a small portion. All of you should not lightly treat this with contempt. If there are further doubts about inclusion, they should soon be settled. You must simply exert strength in practice so that it does not cease through future ages. This matter must not be negligently divulged. If you meet one of pure reflection, that is a rare vessel; it also should not be concealed.

text_zh: 逐位頌竝注別揀
text_en: Verses on each position, with notes and separate selections Bias within the upright. Selection says: a clever head in the dark.

text_zh: 正中偏　揀云。暗裡黠頭。

text_en: What are those teachers? He said: The six sense-fields. What is the place where those teachers fall? He said: A field- hut old man entering the village, with eyes, ears, nose, and tongue all lost. What is meant by your also falling along? He said: Preserving. Preserving what? He said: Do not stir or touch it, yet do not depart from sounds and forms. Also Guishan said: After I pass away, I will become a water buffalo. On its left flank will be written one line of characters: Monk So-and-so of Guishan. Tell me, when you see it, what will you call it? There was no answer. Later Caoshan answered in place: Call it a water buffalo. Asked: Does this water buffalo still know how to plow and farm? He said: Certainly. What kind is it? He said: One wearing hair and horns. In the four seasons, what water and grass does it eat? He said: That which does not enter the mouth. What is the water buffalo? He said: It does not certify to sagehood. What is holding a single stalk of grass? He said: Going where hair, feathers, and roots are alike. Is that transcending saints or transcending kinds? He said: It is transcending saints. Asked: What is the water buffalo? He said: Dark and dim, obscure and murky. What is holding in the mouth a stalk of grass and coming? He said: The ancients already said it: go where hair and feathers are alike. It is also said: One stalk of grass simply clarifies the unchanging. It is also said: Patriarchs Heyu himself stated this as a reply to an old saying What can be done and Buddhas do not know of it, yet the civet-cat and white ox do know. Why do the civet-cat and white ox know of it? He said: Simply because they understand nothing at all. Then why do patriarchs and Buddhas not know of it? He said: Patriarchs are attached to the seal; Buddhas are likeness. As for the civet-cat and white ox, what is it that they know? He said: They only know the civet-cat and white ox. What is the matter known by the civet-cat and white ox? He said: It does not come from west or east. It is not obtained from the thirty-two marks. What is the patriarch? He said: There is above. What is the Buddha? He said: A likeness, and off it goes.

text_en: different kinds within birth and death to gather in others. Though having realized the fruit of nirvana, one does not abandon the realm of birth and death, benefiting oneself and benefiting others, vowing that all sentient beings without exception become Buddhas, while I myself from the very last will become Buddha only afterward. Therefore, if a great bodhisattva of skillful means does not first transform sentient beings, his own matter has no way to be completed. Thus Nanquan said: First cross over there and know that there is, then come back to this side and set your pack in motion. It is also said: A bodhisattva possesses the six perfections and ten thousand practices. text_en: One loses utterly all present worldly and holy causes and effects and virtuous practices; only then does one accord with the one body. text_zh: 僧舉似。洞山大師因僧問沙門行。大師曰。頭 長三尺頸短二寸。此意如何新古兩本無有別異余曰。勝 句妙句。喚什麼作勝句妙句。余曰。勝句妙句 有三種。一者世尊出世。四十九年施設方便。 十二分教。百千三昧妙門。門門穿究。盡是 勝句妙句。此是出世邊說。二者從凡入聖。洞 達自己。與佛無異。得無遺漏。始得通身。始喚 作一塵一念十方婆伽梵一路涅槃門。到恁 麼時節。不處正位。不擇其身。却入異類中。披 毛戴角無異念。故云。一切物類比況不得。諸 佛諸祖計挍不成。所以古人道沙門語不得 將尺寸語與人。故喚作勝句妙句。此是色類 邊語。三者一切所有底物比不得。始呼為勝 句妙句。所以古人道千般比不得。萬物況不 成。智者不能知。上根亦不識。亦云本來無 相似。故勝句妙句。勝句妙句者。天上人間測 度不得底事。故古人云喚作超始終句。借此 為語類邊說行至下益詳稠布衲問。如何是色類。 余曰。披毛戴角。如何是語類。曰曹山只有一 雙眉。如何是水牯牛。曰矇矇瞳瞳。此意如 何。曰不知有天地。

What is called a surpassing phrase, a wondrous phrase. I said, surpassing and wondrous phrases have three kinds. First, the World-Honored One appeared in the world and for forty-nine years set forth expedient means. The twelve divisions of teaching, the hundred thousand samadhi wondrous gates, penetrating each gate to the end, all are surpassing phrases and wondrous phrases. This is speech from the side of transcendence. Second, going from ordinary to holy, thoroughly penetrating oneself and being no different from Buddha, attaining no remainder or leakage, only then attaining the whole body, only then called one mote, one thought, the ten-direction Bhagavans, one road, the gate of nirvana. When one reaches such a time, one does not abide in the proper position and does not choose one’s body, but instead enters the other kind, wearing fur and bearing horns without a thought of difference. Therefore it is said, no class of things can compare with it. All Buddhas and patriarchs cannot reckon or measure it. Therefore the ancients said, in śramaṇa speech one must not use measurements and dimensions to speak to people. Therefore it is called a surpassing phrase, a wondrous phrase. This is on the side of form-kind speech. Third, when nothing whatsoever can be compared to it, only then is it called a surpassing phrase, a wondrous phrase. Therefore the ancients said, a thousand kinds cannot compare, and the ten thousand things cannot illustrate it. The wise cannot know it; those of highest capacity also do not recognize it. It is also said to be originally without likeness. Therefore it is a surpassing phrase, a wondrous phrase. A surpassing phrase, a wondrous phrase, is that which heaven and humanity cannot measure. It is a matter beyond measurement. Therefore the ancients called it the phrase surpassing beginning and end. text_en: buffalo. What is the water buffalo. He said, dim and muddled-eyed. What is the meaning of this. He said, it only thinks of water and grass and knows nothing else. What side-matter does that accomplish. He said, it is simply meeting grass and eating grass, meeting water and drinking water. The Master again said, this saying has force. If you wish to know its force, this person does not cling to matters on the śramaṇa side, nor does he enter the various holy reward positions. This is precisely entering the other kind. This other kind is wearing fur and bearing horns, called śramaṇa practice. It is also called the baggage-place of śramaṇa practice. It is also called head three feet long, neck two inches short. If you wish to know this meaning, when one comes to śramaṇa practice one does not wish to use measurements to divide near and far. One must not speak of Zhang Three or Li Four. And head three feet long means one only reaches it by going from small to great, and today the work is complete. When one reaches such a time, it is called a surpassing phrase, a wondrous phrase. Neck two inches short means not sitting in the śramaṇa position, and also not abiding in the various holy reward positions. Therefore it is neck two inches short. At such a time one must not speak in terms of fitting or not fitting. Therefore it is said, do not bring measurements here to calculate and think. Even so, this is still a matter on the side of kind. You must know there is a matter within the other kind. Did you not see it said: where knowledge does not reach, one must not speak of it. If spoken of, then horns sprout. Calling it suchness is already change. One must proceed within the other kind. This is called the empty one position. It is called face-to-face carrying both. It is wholly without fixed marks. Asked, what is kind. He said, wearing fur and bearing horns. What is the different. He said, what to do, what to do. What is practice. He said, if you want your head, then chop it off and take it away. As for the other kind, what side-matter does it accomplish. He said, this matter has two kinds of other-kind. One is śramaṇa other-kind. The second is situational other-kind. Situational other-kind is the civet-cat and white ox, that sort of thing. As for śramaṇa other-kind, one gains freedom wherever one touches, and only then does one become unchanging. It is not like that other one. My former teacher asked me, where are you going. I said, to the unchanging place. He further said, this unchanging matter has two kinds. First, every person has the fundamental matter. Second, a person who knows this does not abandon any sounds, forms, rights and wrongs, and is not stuck on any thing whatsoever. This is called unchanging in every place. It is also called wearing fur and bearing horns. It is also called entering mud and entering water. Probably a difference in the departing-tone pronunciation It is also called a fellow of the traveling gear. Asked, what is entering mud and entering water. He said, not changing. Does he turn the body or not. He said, he does not turn the body. What are this person’s household matters. He said, the various sages cannot measure them. Why can they not measure them. He said, because he is not the same as the various sages. This is still a matter on the side of kind. Is there still a higher matter. He said, yes. What is the higher matter. He said, if I tell you, I fear it will fall onto the side of kind.

text_en: Third, Lamp-Lighting The Master said, as for before Lamp-Lighting, there are two kinds. First, not yet knowing there is, the same as the blood of kind.

text_zh: 師曰。謂然燈前有二種。一未知有。同於類血 之乳。二知有。猶如意未萌時得本物。此名然 燈前。一種知有。往來言語聲色是非。亦不屬 正照用。亦不得記。同類血之乳。是漏失邊事。 此名然燈後。直是三際事盡。表裏情忘。得無 間斷。此始得名正然燈。乃云得記。
text_en: milk. Second is knowing that there is, like obtaining the original thing before intention has even sprouted. This is called the Lamp-Before. Before the Lamp. One kind of knowing that there is, in comings and goings, speech, sounds, forms, and right and wrong, also does not belong to the functioning of correct illumination, and also does not receive prediction. It is like blood in the same class as milk. This is a matter on the side of leakage and loss. This is called the Lamp-After. It is simply that the affairs of the three times are exhausted, inner and outer sentiments are forgotten, and one attains no interruption. Only then does it first deserve the name of the true Lamp-Lighting, and thus it is said to receive prediction.
